## Recommendation in one box

**Calibrate every model slot (a11–a15) by MAXIMISING the equally weighted average of the two
metrics that will be reported:**

$$
\mathcal{O} \;=\; 0.5\,\mathrm{KGE}\!\left(Q_{\text{sim}},Q_{\text{obs}}\right)
            \;+\; 0.5\,\mathrm{NSE}\!\left(Q_{\text{sim}},Q_{\text{obs}}\right)
$$

on **untransformed** daily flow (mm/day), KGE as defined by @gupta2009 and NSE by @nash1970
(the project's canonical `src/common/metrics.py`), evaluated on the **calibration metric window
1952-10-01 … 1988-09-30 (13 149 days)**, warm-up 1951-10-01 … 1952-09-30 excluded.
Optimisers that minimise use the cost $1-\mathcal{O}$ (perfect = 0, unbounded above).
Implementation: `src.common.metrics_extra.objective` / `objective_cost`; contract:
`config/metrics.yaml`.

*No transform and therefore no offset $\varepsilon$ anywhere.* Observed $Q\ge0.069$ mm/day on all
14 610 days, so $\sqrt{\cdot}$, $\log$ and Box–Cox **would** be defined without an arbitrary
constant (@sec-why) — the point is that they are not needed: a third $\mathrm{KGE}(\sqrt{Q})$ term
was tested explicitly and changed every out-of-sample number by less than 0.001.

*Why not plain KGE, the ranking metric?* Because @sec-transfer calibrates two surrogate
rainfall–runoff models under **24 candidate objectives** on **four independent splits inside the
calibration period** (three of them 20–46 % wetter than their training years, mimicking the
evaluation window, which is 29 % wetter than calibration). Result, as mean shortfall behind the
best objective of each of the 8 experiments ("regret"):

| objective used for calibration | regret in KGE | regret in NSE | worst case KGE | worst case NSE |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **0.5·KGE + 0.5·NSE (recommended)** | 0.026 | 0.017 | **0.056** | **0.047** |
| KGE alone | **0.020** | 0.047 | 0.039 | 0.162 |
| NSE alone | 0.052 | **0.003** | 0.107 | 0.010 |
| KGE(√Q) | 0.024 | 0.019 | 0.067 | 0.063 |

KGE alone and NSE alone each win *their own* metric and lose badly on the other; the 50/50 average
is the only candidate whose **worst case stays below 0.06 on both metrics simultaneously**. KGE and
NSE are not redundant on this record — their Spearman rank correlation over behavioural simulations
is ≈0.7 (@fig-objcorr) — so the average is a genuine compromise rather than a re-weighting.

Trainable models (a09, LSTM) minimise the identical quantity as a **full-batch** loss
(population standard deviations); a per-mini-batch KGE is a different objective.

**Reported metrics are fixed and are NOT chosen here:** a16 reports **KGE and NSE on untransformed
$Q$** only, ranked by KGE, per `config/project.yaml`.
:::

# Scope and constraints {#sec-scope}

The metrics in the *final* report are fixed by the user and by `config/project.yaml`
(`evaluation_protocol.required_metrics: [KGE, NSE]`, `primary_selection_metric: KGE`,
`final_report_metrics_only: true`). Agent 4 therefore does **not** choose the reporting metrics.
What Agent 4 chooses is the **calibration objective**: the scalar that a10's optimisers and
a11–a15's calibration runs drive to its optimum. Objective $\ne$ reporting metric is a deliberate
and well-documented distinction [@clark2021; @mizukami2019]: the objective is an *estimator design
choice* whose only job is to put parameters where the reported metrics will be good **on data the
calibration never saw**.

Three hard boundary conditions frame the choice:

| # | Constraint | Consequence for the objective |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Report = KGE and NSE on raw $Q$; KGE decides the ranking | The objective must be dominated by an untransformed KGE term; an objective built purely on transformed flows optimises the wrong thing |
| 2 | Evaluation window (1949-01-01…1951-09-30) is the **wettest** stretch of the record: mean $Q$ 1.749 vs 1.353 mm/d (ratio 1.29), runoff ratio 0.41 vs 0.35, 1.7 % of days above the calibration $Q_{99}$, but max 45.9 mm/d **below** the calibration max 64.0 mm/d | No magnitude extrapolation is needed, but the objective must not buy calibration score by over-fitting the few largest floods, and must control the volume ratio $\beta$, which is what shifts under a wet transfer |
| 3 | Only 92 warm-up days precede the evaluation metric window | Objectives that depend on long-memory low-flow behaviour (log, $1/Q$) are the most exposed to initial-state error early in 1949 |

: Boundary conditions imposed on the objective choice. {#tbl-constraints}

# Catalogue of metrics {#sec-catalogue}

All formulas use $s_i$ = simulated and $o_i$ = observed daily flow (mm/day), $i=1\dots n$ over the
metric window, $\mu$ = mean, $\sigma$ = standard deviation (population), $r$ = Pearson correlation.
Every metric listed here is implemented in `src/common/metrics_extra.py` and registered in
`mx.METRICS`, with `mx.ORIENTATION` (+1 larger-is-better, −1 smaller-is-better, 0 target-value) and
`mx.OPTIMUM`. `KGE` and `NSE` themselves are imported from the canonical `src/common/metrics.py`.

## Squared-error family

$$
\mathrm{MSE}=\frac1n\sum (s_i-o_i)^2,\qquad \mathrm{RMSE}=\sqrt{\mathrm{MSE}},\qquad
\mathrm{NSE}=1-\frac{\sum (s_i-o_i)^2}{\sum (o_i-\mu_o)^2}
$$

$$
\mathrm{NSE}_{T}=1-\frac{\sum (T(s_i)-T(o_i))^2}{\sum (T(o_i)-\mu_{T(o)})^2},\quad
T\in\{\sqrt{\cdot},\ \log,\ 1/\cdot,\ \text{Box–Cox}_\lambda\},\qquad
\mathrm{NNSE}=\frac{1}{2-\mathrm{NSE}}
$$

@gupta2009 decomposition, used throughout this report:
$$
\mathrm{NSE}=2\alpha r-\alpha^2-\beta_n^2,\qquad
\alpha=\frac{\sigma_s}{\sigma_o},\quad \beta_n=\frac{\mu_s-\mu_o}{\sigma_o}.
$$

## Information-theoretic and probabilistic scores
Mutual information $I(s;o)$, CRPS and Wasserstein distances were considered. CRPS requires a
predictive *distribution*; all five model slots are deterministic and the final ranking is
deterministic, so CRPS is only meaningful if an ensemble is submitted — it is therefore not part of
the objective and not part of the report. The 1-Wasserstein distance between FDCs **is** implemented
(`FDC_W1_log`) because it is a pure distribution-shape diagnostic: a model can have $W_1=0$ and
$r=0$, which makes it a clean complement to KGE's $r$ term. Mutual information was rejected as an
objective: on 13 149 daily values it needs binning/KDE choices that are themselves tuning
parameters, and it is invariant to any monotone transform — including a 50 % volume bias.
:::

**Fact 1 — one per cent of the days own the squared-error criterion.** In the calibration metric
window the wettest 1 % of days (131 of 13 149) carry 15.7 % of the volume but **58.3 %** of
$\sum(o-\mu_o)^2$; the wettest 5 % carry 83.6 %. Any SSE-based objective (MSE, RMSE, NSE, Gaussian
likelihood — all with the same argmax) is therefore, in effect, fitted to ~130 flood days.
The $\sqrt{\cdot}$ transform reduces the 1 % share to 26.8 % and $\log$ to 8.7 %: these numbers,
not a preference, are what "balancing high and low flows" means here.

**Fact 2 — NSE is nearly blind to volume bias at this CV, KGE is not.** For a simulation with the
right shape but a volume ratio $\beta=c$ ($r=1$, $\alpha=c$),

$$
\mathrm{KGE}=1-\sqrt2\,|c-1| \quad\text{(both } \alpha \text{ and } \beta \text{ terms)},\qquad
\mathrm{NSE}=1-\Big(\tfrac{c-1}{\mathrm{CV}_o}\Big)^2\ \text{if only the mean is wrong},
$$

and $\mathrm{CV}_o=2.107$ here.

A model that is 10 % too wet loses **0.100 KGE but only 0.0023 NSE** — a factor 44. This is the
single most important asymmetry for this project: calibrating on NSE lets the optimiser trade
water balance for a slightly better fit to floods almost for free, and that debt is paid in full in
the KGE ranking — *and it is paid on a period 29 % wetter than the one the trade was made on.*
The same algebra explains why KGE″ [@tang2021], whose bias term is $\beta_n=(\mu_s-\mu_o)/\sigma_o$,
behaves almost like NSE here: at CV = 2.107 it divides the bias by 2.1 before squaring it.

What the fingerprint says, in the order that matters for the decision:

1. **Volume bias.** ±20 % volume costs KGE 0.283 but NSE only 0.049 — the algebra of @tbl-bias-sens
   confirmed empirically. log-NSE (0.97) and sqrt-NSE (0.97) are even blinder. Only the KGE family,
   PBIAS/VE and FHV react properly.
2. **Timing.** A one-day shift costs NSE 0.220 but KGE only 0.110 (KGE loses only through $r$).
   NSE is the stronger timing criterion; KGE is the stronger water-balance criterion. They are
   complementary, which is exactly why the project reports both.
3. **Variance errors.** Inflating the variance in log space by 30 % gives KGE −1.17 and NSE −3.27
   while **log-NSE stays at 0.910 and KGE_log at 0.700**. A log-based objective literally cannot see
   a catastrophic error in the raw-flow variance — a decisive argument against calibrating on
   $\log Q$ when the report is on raw $Q$ [@santos2018].
4. **Low-flow instability.** Adding 0.3 mm/d of white noise (a trivial error at flood flows) leaves
   KGE at 0.976 but drives log-NSE to −1.50 and inverse-NSE to −15 554. Inverse and log objectives
   are numerically dominated by the smallest flows of a perennial river; they are unusable as a
   primary objective here and are kept only as diagnostics.
5. **Over-smoothing** (7-day moving average, i.e. a model with too much storage) is punished by
   KGE (0.785 via $\alpha$ = 0.81) and by FHV (−20 %) but barely by log-NSE (0.913) — another
   transform-blindness.
6. **Peak truncation** (top 2 % cut by 30 %) costs KGE 0.229 and NSE 0.074 but *improves* log-NSE
   and inverse-NSE to ≈1.00. FHV = −27.6 % detects it cleanly, which is why FHV is retained as the
   mandatory high-flow diagnostic.

# Experiment 2 — which objective transfers best to an independent, wetter period? {#sec-transfer}

This is the decision-relevant experiment. @sec-synthetic shows what a metric *sees*; it does not
show what happens when a metric is *optimised*. Here two surrogate rainfall–runoff models are
calibrated with 24 candidate objectives and the resulting parameter sets are scored with the
**reported** metrics (KGE, NSE on raw $Q$) on data withheld from that calibration.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Lane and leakage statement
The two models below are **experimental surrogates internal to this report**, not project model
slots (those are a03/a05–a09's outputs; nothing is written to `src/models/`). Every split used here
lives strictly inside the calibration window; `src.common.data.slice_run(df, "evaluation")` is never
called and `LR_AGENT` is never set. The evaluation window contributes nothing — not even a summary
statistic — to the objective choice.
:::

## Design

* **Surrogate 1 — HyMOD** (5 parameters: $C_{max}$, $b_{exp}$, $\alpha$, $R_s$, $R_q$): a PDM
  storage [@moore1985] feeding one slow and three quick linear reservoirs. HyMOD *is* the classic
  Leaf River model [@boyle2000; @vrugt2003], which makes it the most defensible surrogate available.
* **Surrogate 2 — NLRes** (5 parameters: $S_{max}$, $\beta$, $d$, $k_f$, $k_s$): HBV-style power-law
  saturation runoff, a linear fast reservoir and a **non-linear** slow reservoir $q=k_sS^{1.5}$,
  chosen because a02 found a non-linear recession (Brutsaert–Nieber $b=1.68$). Two structurally
  different surrogates guard against a conclusion that is an artefact of one model.
* **Optimiser:** SciPy `differential_evolution`, seed 42, popsize 15, maxiter 150, tol $10^{-8}$,
  polish — identical budget for every objective, so differences are attributable to the objective.
* **Splits (all inside calibration):**

from numba import njit, prange

@njit(cache=True, fastmath=True)
def _hymod(P, E, cmax, bexp, alpha, Rs, Rq):
    n = P.shape[0]; Q = np.empty(n)
    x_loss = 0.0; x_slow = 2.3503 / (Rs * 22.5); x_q1 = x_q2 = x_q3 = 0.0
    b1 = bexp + 1.0; cm_b = cmax / b1
    for t in range(n):
        Pval = P[t]; PETval = E[t]; xn_prev = x_loss
        arg = 1.0 - b1 * xn_prev / cmax
        if arg < 0.0: arg = 0.0
        ct_prev = cmax * (1.0 - arg ** (1.0 / b1))
        UT1 = Pval - cmax + ct_prev
        if UT1 < 0.0: UT1 = 0.0
        Pval = Pval - UT1
        dummy = (ct_prev + Pval) / cmax
        if dummy > 1.0: dummy = 1.0
        xn = cm_b * (1.0 - (1.0 - dummy) ** b1)
        UT2 = Pval - (xn - xn_prev)
        if UT2 < 0.0: UT2 = 0.0
        evap = (1.0 - (cm_b - xn) / cm_b) * PETval
        if evap > xn: evap = xn
        x_loss = xn - evap
        UQ = alpha * (UT1 + UT2); US = (1.0 - alpha) * (UT1 + UT2)
        x_slow = (1.0 - Rs) * x_slow + (1.0 - Rs) * US; QS = (Rs / (1.0 - Rs)) * x_slow
        x_q1 = (1.0 - Rq) * x_q1 + (1.0 - Rq) * UQ;  o1 = (Rq / (1.0 - Rq)) * x_q1
        x_q2 = (1.0 - Rq) * x_q2 + (1.0 - Rq) * o1;  o2 = (Rq / (1.0 - Rq)) * x_q2
        x_q3 = (1.0 - Rq) * x_q3 + (1.0 - Rq) * o2;  o3 = (Rq / (1.0 - Rq)) * x_q3
        q = QS + o3
        Q[t] = q if q > 1e-9 else 1e-9
    return Q

@njit(cache=True, fastmath=True)
def _nlres(P, E, Smax, beta, d, kf, ks):
    n = P.shape[0]; Q = np.empty(n)
    S = 0.5 * Smax; Sf = 0.0; Ss = 10.0
    for t in range(n):
        p = P[t]; ratio = S / Smax
        if ratio > 1.0: ratio = 1.0
        r = p * ratio ** beta
        S = S + p - r
        ea = E[t] * (S / Smax)
        if ea > S: ea = S
        S = S - ea
        if S > Smax:
            r += S - Smax; S = Smax
        Sf = Sf + d * r; qf = kf * Sf; Sf = Sf - qf
        Ss = Ss + (1.0 - d) * r; qs = ks * Ss ** 1.5
        if qs > Ss: qs = Ss
        Ss = Ss - qs
        q = qf + qs
        Q[t] = q if q > 1e-9 else 1e-9
    return Q

@njit(parallel=True, cache=True)
def simulate_batch(P, E, theta, which):
    ns = theta.shape[0]; nt = P.shape[0]; out = np.empty((ns, nt))
    for i in prange(ns):
        if which == 0:
            out[i] = _hymod(P, E, theta[i, 0], theta[i, 1], theta[i, 2], theta[i, 3], theta[i, 4])
        else:
            out[i] = _nlres(P, E, theta[i, 0], theta[i, 1], theta[i, 2], theta[i, 3], theta[i, 4])
    return out

from scipy.optimize import differential_evolution

def optimise(mask, which, fobj, seed=SEED, maxiter=150, popsize=15):
    b = BOUNDS[which]; o = OBS[mask]
    def cost(th):
        s = simulate_batch(P, PET, np.atleast_2d(th), which)[0]
        v = fobj(s[mask], o)

    res = differential_evolution(cost, list(map(tuple, b)), seed=seed, maxiter=maxiter,
                                 popsize=popsize, tol=1e-8, mutation=(0.3, 1.0),
                                 recombination=0.9, polish=True, init="sobol", workers=1)
    return res.x, -res.fun

## The decision

**Calibrate on $\mathcal{O}=0.5\,\mathrm{KGE}(Q)+0.5\,\mathrm{NSE}(Q)$ — maximise — on
1952-10-01…1988-09-30; equivalently minimise $1-\mathcal{O}$.**

This is *not* the answer the catalogue alone would have suggested (a KGE + $\sqrt{Q}$ composite);
it is what @sec-transfer produced. The decisive numbers:

| Criterion | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **Alignment with the reported metrics** | The objective *is* the unweighted average of the two reported metrics on untransformed $Q$ — nothing is optimised that is not reported, and nothing reported is left out. No transform, no $\varepsilon$, no tuning constant other than the 50/50 weight. |
| **The two terms are not redundant** | Over 6 000 behavioural HyMOD simulations the Spearman rank correlation between KGE and NSE is only ≈0.7 (@fig-objcorr): KGE and NSE genuinely disagree about which parameter set is better on this record, so averaging them is a real multi-criteria compromise, not a re-scaling. |
| **Robustness to the skew and to volume bias** | KGE's $\beta$ term supplies the water-balance control that NSE lacks at CV = 2.107 (factor 14–89, @tbl-bias-sens), while NSE's stronger timing sensitivity (@sec-synthetic item 2) compensates KGE's weaker one. The pair covers each other's blind spots. |
| **Transfer to a wetter period** | @tbl-regret: worst-case regret 0.056 (KGE) and 0.047 (NSE) — the only candidate of the 24 that keeps **both** below 0.06. KGE-only calibration has a worst case of 0.162 in NSE, NSE-only 0.107 in KGE. On the wet blocks the recommendation reaches mean KGE 0.773 / NSE 0.725 against 0.783/0.697 (KGE-only) and 0.743/0.734 (NSE-only): it gives up ≈0.010 KGE to gain ≈0.028 NSE. |
| **Parsimony** | Three further variants were run through all 8 experiments: $(\mathrm{KGE}+\mathrm{NSE}+\mathrm{KGE}(\sqrt Q))/3$, $0.4/0.4/0.2$ and $0.7\,\mathrm{KGE}+0.3\,\mathrm{NSE}$. The first two are indistinguishable from the recommendation (all out-of-sample means differ by < 0.001); the 70/30 weighting trades 0.004 KGE for 0.008 NSE and doubles the worst case. The simplest member of the tied group wins. |
| **Optimiser and ML compatibility** | Smooth, bounded above by 1, ~0.9 ms per evaluation on 13 149 days, and differentiable everywhere — a10's global searches, a11–a15's calibrations and a09's gradient training all use the *same* scalar. |

::: {.callout-note}
## Honest limitation
The recommendation does **not** improve low flows: out-of-sample log-NSE on the wet blocks is 0.666
for the recommendation against 0.761 for sqrt-NSE and 0.591 for KGE-only, and the high-flow bias FHV
is −16.9 % against −12.3 % for KGE-only. Balancing the hydrograph and maximising the two reported
metrics are different goals, and `config/project.yaml` asks for the second. The low-flow and
high-flow behaviour is therefore controlled through the *acceptance checks* in
`config/metrics.yaml` (`|PBIAS| ≤ 10 %`, $\beta\in[0.90,1.10]$, $\alpha\in[0.85,1.15]$,
$|\mathrm{FHV}| \le 25$ %, $|\Delta\mathrm{BFI}|\le0.15$), which a11–a15 must report, not through
the objective. A slot that passes the acceptance checks *and* maximises $\mathcal{O}$ is both
hydrologically sound and competitive in the ranking.
:::

## Why not each alternative

* **Plain KGE (2009).** The ranking metric, and the declared fallback. It gives the best
  out-of-sample KGE (regret 0.020 vs 0.026) — but the worst NSE of the whole KGE family
  (regret 0.047, worst case 0.162, wet-block NSE 0.697). Since NSE is reported too, paying
  0.006 KGE to remove that exposure is the better bet.
* **NSE.** Nearly blind to volume bias at CV = 2.107 (@tbl-bias-sens): a 10 % volume error costs
  0.0023 NSE and 0.100 KGE. NSE-only calibrations produced the largest $|\beta-1|$ on every wet
  test block (mean $\beta$ = 1.103 vs 1.089) and the largest KGE regret (0.052). Never alone.
* **RMSE / MSE / Gaussian likelihood.** Monotone transformations of each other and of NSE for a
  fixed observation window — identical argmax, identical weakness. Not separate options.
  (`LL_bc025` and `NSE_bc025` returned bit-identical parameter sets in @tbl-transfer-temporal,
  which is the empirical demonstration of that equivalence.)
* **KGE′ (2012).** $\gamma=\mathrm{CV}_s/\mathrm{CV}_o$ cancels a pure scaling error, so a uniformly
  biased model is penalised once instead of twice. It wins single wet blocks (KGE 0.909 on
  WY1961–63) but has the worst NSE regret of the KGE family (0.118) and out-of-sample log-NSE 0.11:
  it buys KGE by wrecking the low-flow end.
* **KGE″ (2021).** Built for $\mu_o\to0$ (ephemeral rivers). At CV = 2.107 it divides the bias by
  2.1 before squaring and degenerates towards NSE; on the temporal split it was strictly worse than
  KGE for both surrogates. Leaf River is perennial — there is nothing to fix.
* **Non-parametric KGE.** Robust and FDC-based, and the best objective for HyMOD on the temporal
  split, but it collapsed for the second surrogate (test NSE 0.257) because it optimises ranks and
  FDC shape rather than event magnitudes. Mean KGE regret 0.077. Retained as a diagnostic.
* **log-NSE / log-KGE / inverse-NSE.** @sec-synthetic items 3–4: they cannot see a 30 % raw-variance
  error and they explode on 0.3 mm/d of low-flow noise. In the transfer experiment KGE_log was the
  worst objective tested (mean KGE regret 0.181, NSE regret 0.579; test NSE −0.47 for one surrogate)
  and inverse-NSE was second worst. With only 92 warm-up days before the evaluation metric window,
  an objective dominated by the slowest store is also the most exposed to initial-state error.
* **MAE.** A genuinely strong performer (best mean test KGE on the temporal split) and robust to the
  tail, but it is not one of the reported metrics, it has no diagnostic decomposition, and its
  worst-case KGE regret (0.091) is 1.6× the recommendation's.
* **Formal likelihoods (GL, AR(1)).** Only justified if a10 chooses DREAM *and* the deliverable were
  predictive uncertainty. They add 3–5 nuisance parameters and, in the Gaussian case, reduce to NSE.
* **Signature / Pareto multi-objective.** A Pareto front cannot be handed to a11–a15 as a single
  number and the final ranking is single-objective by construction. Signatures are used as
  acceptance checks instead (@sec-a16).

## Per-slot guidance

| Slot | Model kind | Objective | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1–5, conceptual (`kind = "conceptual"`) | global search (a10) | maximise `mx.objective` $=0.5\,\mathrm{KGE}(Q)+0.5\,\mathrm{NSE}(Q)$, equivalently minimise `mx.objective_cost` | identical for every slot — otherwise a comparison between slots is not a comparison of models. Map non-finite costs to $10^6$. |
| trainable / ML (`kind = "trainable"`, e.g. LSTM) | gradient descent | minimise `1 - objective` as a **full-batch** loss on the training mask, in torch with population sd (`unbiased=False`); the mini-batch NSE\* of @kratzert2019 may be used as the *inner* loss for stability, but early stopping and model selection use the composite on the internal-validation mask | KGE needs the whole batch: $\mu$, $\sigma$ and $r$ are not additive over mini-batches |
| ensembles / hybrids | weights fitted on calibration only | same objective; weights fitted on the internal-validation mask (1981-10-01…1988-09-30) and then frozen | `config/project.yaml`: ensemble weights must never see evaluation data |

Fallback if a slot's optimiser cannot handle the composite (a11–a15 must log this in their handoff):
use plain **KGE (2009)** and report the difference. Do **not** fall back to NSE alone.

   period cost ΔKGE −0.077 and ΔNSE −0.054. A large drop on the evaluation window should therefore
   be read as over-fitting or a warm-up artefact, not as "the evaluation period is wetter".
5. **Expect the volume ratio to fall.** Across the three wet blocks $\beta$ dropped by
   **−0.068** relative to its value on the training years (and rose by +0.108 in the dry
   direction), with $\alpha$ moving the same way. On a 29 %-wetter evaluation window a $\beta$
   of 0.93–1.00 for a model calibrated to $\beta\approx1.03$ is the *expected* outcome. This is a
   prediction to be checked, **not** a correction: no model may be re-tuned for it, and no
   statistic of the evaluation window may enter any calibration.
6. **Only 92 warm-up days** precede the evaluation metric window (against 366 in calibration), so
   the initial-state choice is visible in Jan–Mar 1949. a16 should state the initialisation used
   and, as a robustness check, report KGE/NSE with the first 30 metric days dropped — as a
   *footnote*, never as the headline number.
7. Diagnostics ($r,\alpha,\beta$, PBIAS, FHV, FLV, log-NSE, BFI) may be computed for the discussion
   but must be visually separated from the ranking table.

written_by: a04-metrics-advisor
written_at: "2026-09-15"

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. What the FINAL report shows. Fixed by the user / config/project.yaml — not Agent 4's choice.
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. THE CALIBRATION OBJECTIVE  (this is what a10/a11–a15 must optimise)

recommended_objective: KGE_NSE_50

objective:
  id: KGE_NSE_50
  name: "Equally weighted average of the two reported efficiencies on untransformed daily flow"
  formula_latex: "\\mathcal{O} = 0.5\\,KGE(Q_{sim},Q_{obs}) + 0.5\\,NSE(Q_{sim},Q_{obs})"
  formula_python: "0.5*kge(sim, obs) + 0.5*nse(sim, obs)"
  kge_variant: "Gupta et al. (2009): 1 - sqrt((r-1)^2 + (alpha-1)^2 + (beta-1)^2), alpha = sd_sim/sd_obs, beta = mean_sim/mean_obs"
  nse_variant: "Nash & Sutcliffe (1970): 1 - sum((sim-obs)^2)/sum((obs-mean_obs)^2)"
  weights: {KGE: 0.5, NSE: 0.5}
  transform:
    name: identity                 # NO transform is applied to sim or obs
    epsilon: 0.0                   # would not be needed anyway: observed Q >= 0.069 mm/day
    epsilon_justification: >
      a02 verified Q > 0 on all 14,610 days (quantised at 0.0012544 mm/day = 1 cfs over
      1,949 km2), so sqrt/log/Box-Cox would be defined without an arbitrary constant. A
      sqrt-KGE third term was nevertheless TESTED (variants KNS_333 and KNS_442 in
      reports/04_metrics.qmd Experiment 2) and changed every out-of-sample number by < 0.001,
      so it was dropped on parsimony grounds. Simulated flows are floored at 1e-12 mm/day only
      to keep diagnostics finite.
  # ---- sign convention -------------------------------------------------------------
  maximise: true                   # the objective is a SCORE: larger is better
  optimum: 1.0                     # perfect simulation
  minimised_quantity: "1 - objective"    # what SCE-UA / DE / Nelder-Mead / L-BFGS must minimise
  minimised_optimum: 0.0
  unbounded_below: true            # can go to -inf
  nan_policy: "non-finite objective -> return cost 1e6 (never NaN) so the optimiser keeps moving"
  # ---- implementation --------------------------------------------------------------
  python:
    module: src.common.metrics_extra
    score: "objective(sim, obs)"          # maximise this
    cost:  "objective_cost(sim, obs)"     # == 1 - objective(sim, obs); minimise this
    constants: {OBJECTIVE_W: 0.5, OBJECTIVE_TRANSFORM: identity, OBJECTIVE_NAME: KGE_NSE_50}
  # ---- period mask -----------------------------------------------------------------
  period:
    which: calibration
    run_window:    ["1951-10-01", "1988-09-30"]   # simulate from here (warm-up included)
    warmup_window: ["1951-10-01", "1952-09-30"]   # 366 d, EXCLUDED from the objective
    metric_window: ["1952-10-01", "1988-09-30"]   # 13,149 d: the objective is computed on THIS
    how: >
      run = src.common.data.slice_run(df, "calibration");
      mask = src.common.data.metric_mask(run, "calibration");
      score = src.common.metrics_extra.objective(sim[mask], obs[mask])
    never_use: "evaluation window 1948-10-01..1951-09-30 (a16 only; LR_AGENT=a16)"
  # ---- internal split (model selection WITHOUT touching evaluation) -----------------

    train:      ["1952-10-01", "1981-09-30"]   # 10,592 d - hyperparameters, early stopping
    validation: ["1981-10-01", "1988-09-30"]   # 2,557 d - model/ensemble selection, ensemble weights

      parameter set; use train/validation only to check for over-fitting and to report a transfer
      number. Trainable models: fit on train, early-stop and select on validation, then optionally
      refit on the full window with the selected hyperparameters. Ensemble weights: fit on
      validation only, then freeze.
  cost_note: "~0.9 ms per evaluation on 13,149 days (one KGE + one NSE, pure NumPy)"
  # ---- evidence --------------------------------------------------------------------

    experiment: "reports/04_metrics.qmd Experiment 2: 2 surrogate models (HyMOD, NLRes) x 4 independent splits inside calibration x 24 candidate objectives, identical DE budget (seed 42)"
    mean_regret_KGE: 0.0259     # mean shortfall behind the best objective of each experiment
    mean_regret_NSE: 0.0165
    worst_case_regret_KGE: 0.0558
    worst_case_regret_NSE: 0.0468
    comparison:

      NSE_only:  {mean_regret_KGE: 0.0521, mean_regret_NSE: 0.0028, worst_case_KGE: 0.1068}

    wet_shift_performance: {KGE_test: 0.773, NSE_test: 0.725, beta: 1.089, alpha: 0.889, FHV_pct: -16.9}
    note: "the three wet-shift splits reproduce the evaluation window's situation (test period 20-46 % wetter than training, test maximum below the training maximum)"

# 3. Loss for trainable / ML models (a09 LSTM and any gradient-trained slot)

trainable_loss:
  id: KGE_NSE_50_loss
  formula: "1 - [0.5*KGE(Q_sim, Q_obs) + 0.5*NSE(Q_sim, Q_obs)]"
  minimise: true
  optimum: 0.0
  batching: full_window           # KGE needs mu, sigma and r over the WHOLE scored window
  reference_numpy: "src.common.metrics_extra.trainable_loss_numpy(sim, obs)"

rejected_objectives:      # tested in reports/04_metrics.qmd Experiment 2 and rejected

    why: >

      calibrations carried the largest |beta-1| into every out-of-sample test (mean KGE regret
      0.052, worst case 0.107). NSE is fine as HALF of the recommended objective, never alone.
  - id: [MSE, RMSE, LL_gauss]
    why: "monotone transformations of NSE for a fixed observation window: identical argmax, identical weakness"
  - id: [NSE_log, KGE_log, NSE_inv]
    why: >

      0.3 mm/d of white noise). KGE_log had by far the worst transfer (mean KGE regret 0.18).

  - id: KGE_2021

  - id: [KNS_333, KNS_442]
